nodes.description: ACTH was followed by resolution of infantile spasms without later seizures in one adult in the broader 2021 CACNA1E cohort. A 2026 mixed-gene retrospective DEE series also included CACNA1E among cases seizure-free at day 14, but its abstract does not provide the CACNA1E variant classification or durable gene-specific outcome. These reports do not establish response rates for DEE69 or variant-specific efficacy.

evidence.snippet: The six individuals harboring the recurrent c.2104G>A (p.Ala702Thr) variant had a relatively homogeneous phenotype that was representative of the overall CACNA1E-encephalopathy phenotype. All individuals had refractory infantile-onset epilepsy, epileptic spasms, severe hypotonia, and profound developmental impairment. Five out of six individuals (83%) harboring the c.2104G>A (p.Ala702Thr) variant had congenital joint contractures and macrocephaly; hypsarrhythmia on EEG consistent with a diagnosis of West syndrome was observed in four of these individuals (67%). Two of these six individuals died in early childhood at ages 1 and 3 years.

nodes.description: Among 18 treated discovery-cohort participants, five were described as having substantial improvement: two remained seizure-free for two and five years, two relapsed after four years and 18 months, and one had a marked reduction but stopped because of sedation. Ten had no effect and three had reductions without seizure freedom. These uncontrolled observations support possible benefit for some patients, not a predictable response or demonstrated developmental rescue. The detailed results are more qualified than the abstract's statement that five achieved seizure freedom.

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Pathogenic Variants in CACNA1E Cause Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy with Contractures, Macrocephaly, and Dyskinesias.
evidence.snippet: Although seizures were resistant to multiple anti-epileptic drugs (AEDs) in most individuals for whom data were available (20/25; 80%), five individuals (1, 15, 16, 21, 27) reported significant improvement in seizure control with topiramate, the only AED noted to have a substantial effect on seizure control in any participants (Table S1).

evidence.reference_title: De Novo Pathogenic Variants in CACNA1E Cause Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy with Contractures, Macrocephaly, and Dyskinesias.
evidence.snippet: Two individuals (16 and 27) remain seizure free for 2 and 5 years, respectively. However, in individuals 15 and 21, seizures eventually recurred after seizure-free periods of 4 years and 18 months, respectively; individual 21 died following an episode of status epilepticus. Individual 1 reported a substantial reduction in seizure frequency with topiramate, but it was discontinued due to increased sedation. Topiramate had no effect on seizure control in 10/18 (56%) individuals who were prescribed it; 3/18 (17%) individuals who were prescribed topiramate reported a reduction in seizures but were never seizure free.

nodes.description: H151L, M163T and R1182C were expressed in human alpha1E-3 with rat beta1b and alpha2delta1. Electrophysiology demonstrates heterogeneous loss of function; these models address broader CACNA1E neurological presentations and do not reproduce the canonical DEE69 gain-of-function mechanism. Structural predictions are not empirical surface-expression measurements.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of Three Distinct Loss-of-Function Cav2.3 Variants.
evidence.snippet: M163T and R1182C exhibit depolarizing shifts in the voltage-dependence of activation, whereas R1182C also shows a reduced peak current density. H151L selectively slows recovery from inactivation.

nodes.description: Phe698Ser, Ile701Val and Ala702Thr in human alpha1E-1 with beta2d were tested with barium as the charge carrier. These assays establish gating effects but do not reproduce native neuronal subunit composition, developmental circuitry or the complete heterozygous state.

nodes.description: Human alpha1E-3 Ile603Leu was expressed with beta1b and alpha2delta1; calcium and barium recordings showed increased density and facilitated activation without altered inactivation. Assay conditions differ from the DII-S6 experiments, precluding simple quantitative comparisons across the two systems.

evidence.snippet: This variant resulted in a massive increase in whole-cell current density (Figures 3 and S2) to a level that in many cases precluded functional biophysical characterization. In a subset of cells where the current could be properly clamped, our analysis revealed a >10 mV hyperpolarizing shift in half activation voltage (Figures 3 and S2; Table 2). There was no significant effect on channel inactivation.

nodes.description: Whole-cell patch clamp of Leu228Pro versus wild type shows hyperpolarized activation and steady-state inactivation, with an expanded window current. Peak density, inactivation kinetics and recovery were unchanged. The published abstract supports these channel findings; neuronal or treatment rescue is not demonstrated.

evidence.reference_title: Gating effects of a Cav2.3 calcium channel variant linked to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: Compared to wild-type, the L228P mutant did not present altered peak current density, inactivation kinetics, or recovery from inactivation, but showed a significant shift towards hyperpolarized voltages in both voltage-dependent activation and steady-state inactivation. This resulted in a broader window current shifted towards more hyperpolarized potentials, which predicts increased channel availability and activity at subthreshold voltages relative to wild-type channels.
